title: Sorted Pair Sum
statement:
Find two positions in a sorted array whose values add up to a target, using only constant extra space.

Contract
- `sorted` is a non-null array in non-decreasing order; it may be empty and values may repeat.
- Return an `int[]` of two different indices `{i, j}` with `i < j` and `sorted[i] + sorted[j] == target`. When several pairs qualify, any one is accepted.
- Return an empty array (length 0) when no such pair exists.
- Add values as `long`, so `int` overflow cannot create or hide a pair. Do not mutate `sorted`; do not allocate a map or copy of the input.

Examples
- `findPair(new int[]{2, 5, 9, 11, 15}, 13)` returns `{0, 3}` (values 2 and 11).
- `findPair(new int[]{4, 4, 9}, 8)` returns `{0, 1}`: the same value may be used twice from different positions.
- `findPair(new int[]{1, 3, 6}, 100)` returns an empty array.
hints: Because the array is sorted, a sum that is too big can only shrink by moving the right end left.
Keep one index at each end. If the sum is below the target advance the left index; if above, retreat the right index; stop when they meet.
Never revisit an index once it is discarded, and add as long values. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the array length.
inputSyntax: Input: the sorted array values, then the target, for example: [2, 5, 9, 11, 15] 13
